Models that do not use time factor as one of their features should not be considered accurate (Fathalla et al., 2020). Once again, more research has been done for the automotive and household markets, where we can observe approaches employing machine learning time series data models predicting second-hand car prices (Sun et al., 2022) or predictions of the price index of second-hand houses with neural networks (Ma et al., 2021; Xu & Zhang, 2022). Regarding used electronics, we can mention standard approaches utilized by Carta et al. (2019) and Fathalla et al. (2023), who both leverage ARIMA models predicting time series values for different Amazon products, e.g. books, electronics or movies and TV. In the area of e-commerce, Osawa et al. (2021) has proposed an ARIMA model trained on the customers’ purchase history including seasonal fluctuations in product prices. In contrast, Smedmark and Filip (2021) suggests neural networks tackle the trend analysis.
